title: AI System — Behavior Trees
description: Reference for the Blastback Engine AI system, covering behavior tree node structure, fields, node types, and the online AI editor.
content:
AI System — Behavior Trees

The Blastback Engine uses a behavior tree (BT) system for AI-driven entity decision making. Behavior trees provide a flexible, hierarchical way to define complex AI behaviors through composable nodes.

To attach a behavior tree to an entity, add the ai component to the entity's components dictionary.

BT Node Schema

Each node in a behavior tree is defined with the following structure:

JSON
{
  "type": "selector",
  "commands": [
    "isPlayerInRange 120",
    "hasLineOfSight"
  ],
  "children": {
    "sequence.chase": {
      "commands": [],
      "children": { ... }
    },
    "action.idle": {
      "commands": []
    }
  },
  "parameters": {
    "cooldown": 2.0
  }
}

Node Fields

NameTypeDescription
typestringThe node type (e.g., "selector", "sequence", "action"). This field is optional — the type can also be inferred from the children dictionary key using the format "type.name".
commandsstring[]An array of command strings that check conditions. These commands are evaluated when the node is reached. If any condition fails, the node returns failure without executing its children.
childrenDictionary<string, BTNode>A dictionary of child nodes. The key follows the format "type.name", where type is the child node's type and name is a descriptive label. This allows defining the child's type inline without an explicit type field.
parametersDictionary<string, Object>Additional parameters for decorator nodes. The available parameters depend on the decorator type (e.g., cooldown, repeatCount, timeout).

The type field and the children key format "type.name" are two ways to specify a node's type. When using the children key format, you can omit the explicit type field on the child node. For example, a child with key "sequence.patrol" is automatically a sequence node named patrol.

Node Types

Composite Nodes

Composite nodes control the flow of execution through their children.

TypeDescription
selectorExecutes children in order until one succeeds. Returns success on the first successful child, or failure if all children fail. Use for "try this, or else try that" logic.
sequenceExecutes children in order until one fails. Returns failure on the first failed child, or success if all children succeed. Use for "do this, then do that" logic.

Leaf Nodes

Leaf nodes perform actual actions or checks.

TypeDescription
actionExecutes a specific action command (e.g., move, attack, wait).
conditionEvaluates a condition and returns success or failure without performing any action.

Decorator Nodes

Decorator nodes wrap a single child and modify its behavior. They use the parameters field for configuration.

TypeParametersDescription
inverter—Inverts the result of its child node (success becomes failure and vice versa).
repeaterrepeatCountRepeats its child node a specified number of times.
cooldowncooldownPrevents the child from being executed again until the cooldown period (in seconds) has elapsed.
timeouttimeoutForces the child to return failure if it does not complete within the specified time (in seconds).

Example: Enemy Patrol and Chase

JSON
{
  "type": "selector",
  "commands": [],
  "children": {
    "sequence.chase": {
      "commands": [
        "isPlayerInRange 150",
        "hasLineOfSight"
      ],
      "children": {
        "action.moveToPlayer": {
          "commands": ["moveToTarget player"]
        },
        "action.attack": {
          "commands": ["useWeapon"]
        }
      }
    },
    "sequence.patrol": {
      "commands": [],
      "children": {
        "action.moveToWaypoint": {
          "commands": ["moveToWaypoint"]
        },
        "action.wait": {
          "commands": ["wait 2.0"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

In this example, the root selector first tries the chase sequence. If the player is in range and visible, the entity moves toward the player and attacks. If the chase conditions fail, the selector falls through to the patrol sequence, where the entity moves between waypoints.

Behavior trees are evaluated every frame. Keep your trees efficient by placing the most likely-to-fail conditions early in sequences and the most common behaviors first in selectors.

Online AI Editor

The Blastback Engine provides a visual behavior tree editor that you can use to design, test, and export AI trees without editing JSON by hand.

Open the Online AI Editor

The online editor allows you to visually construct behavior trees with drag-and-drop nodes, test them in real time, and export the result as JSON that you can paste directly into your entity's ai component definition.
